We employ domain-specific encoders to project these heterogeneous data into a triplet { 𝐩 i , 𝐠 i , 𝐭 i } \{\mathbf{p}_{i},\mathbf{g}_{i},\mathbf{t}_{i}\} . Figure 1: The proposed Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni framework. Omni-modal inputs are embedded via domain-specific encoders then fused by Synergistic Information Bottleneck (SIB) module into a compact joint representation. The Φ ​ ID \mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID} objective regularizes the omni-modal latent space, explicitly expanding emergent synergy while compressing redundancy. For inference, the frozen Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni slide encoder enables robust unimodal few-shot adaption. Pathological slide encoder. Given a WSI 𝐗 p ( i ) ∈ ℝ d x × d y × 3 \mathbf{X}_{p}^{(i)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}\times d_{y}\times 3} for the i th i^{\text{th}} patient, we tessellate it into 256 × \times 256 patches at 20 × \times using TRIDENT [ 30 ] and extract it into patch embeddings using UNIv2 [ 2 ] as 𝐏 i ∈ ℝ D p × 1536 \mathbf{P}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{D}_{p}\times 1536} . These embeddings are then aggregated by a slide encoder f MIL f^{\text{MIL}} , implemented as an ABMIL [ 6 ] with a pre-attention layer [ 8 ] , mapping the patch set into a slide embedding 𝐩 i ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{p}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} . Transcriptomics encoder. We utilized paired Bulk RNA-seq data from UCSC Xena after log2(x+1) and RSEM transformed [ 5 ] .

We select the genes associated with 50 MsigDB [ 11 ] Hallmark biological pathways to construct an input profile 𝐆 i ∈ ℝ D g ​ ( D g ≈ 5000 ) \mathbf{G}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathrm{D}_{g}}(\mathrm{D}_{g}\approx 5000) , then encode it into a transcriptomics embedding 𝐠 i ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{g}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} through a two-layer multilayer perceptron (MLP). Text report encoder. We processed pathology reports via an OCR-based pipeline with text cleaning [ 21 ] (removing diagnostic labels). We encode the extracted text into semantic features 𝐓 i ∈ ℝ 1024 \mathbf{T}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{1024} via pre-trained GatorTron [ 29 ] , and further project it into a text report embedding 𝐭 i ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{t}_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} via a two-layer MLP. 2.2 Synergistic Information Bottleneck Module A key challenge in multimodal learning lies in the modality gap : naive integration propagates noise and enables dominant modality to suppress weaker ones. To address this, we propose the Synergistic Information Bottleneck (SIB) module to distill high-order cross-modal interactions. Structurally, SIB serves as an inductive bottleneck that maps the concatenated unimodal embeddings 𝐗 joint ∈ ℝ 3 ​ d \mathbf{X}_{\text{joint}}\in\mathbb{R}^{3d} to a compact joint representation 𝐙 mm ∈ ℝ d \mathbf{Z}_{\text{mm}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} via linear projection layers Proj ⁡ ( ⋅ ) \mathrm{Proj}(\cdot) : 𝐙 mm = ℱ SIB ​ ( 𝐗 joint ) ​ = △ ​ LN ​ ( Proj 2 ​ ( ReLU ​ ( Proj 1 ​ [ 𝐩 i ⊕ 𝐠 i ⊕ 𝐭 i ] ) ) ) \mathbf{Z}_{\text{mm}}=\mathcal{F}_{\text{SIB}}\bigl(\mathbf{X}_{\text{joint}}\bigr)\overset{\triangle}{=}\mathrm{LN}\big(\mathrm{Proj}_{2}\left(\text{ReLU}(\mathrm{Proj}_{1}[\mathbf{p}_{i}\oplus\mathbf{g}_{i}\oplus\mathbf{t}_{i}])\right)\big) (1) where ⊕ \oplus and LN \mathrm{LN} denote concatenation and Layer Normalization.

By creating a dimensionality bottleneck ( Proj 1 → Proj 2 : 3 ​ d → 2 ​ d → d \mathrm{Proj}_{1}\to\mathrm{Proj}_{2}:3d\to 2d\to d ), SIB constrains the capacity of the multimodal transition, effectively filtering out modality-specific noise while capturing the most informative synergistic diagnostic signals. 2.3 Synergistic Information Disentanglement ( Φ ​ ID \mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID} ) Mutual information. The core objective of multimodal learning is to maximize the dependency between input modalities 𝐗 \mathbf{X} and the fused feature 𝐙 \mathbf{Z} , typically measured via Mutual Information (MI) ℐ ⁡ ( 𝐗 , 𝐙 ) \mathcal{I}(\mathbf{X};\mathbf{Z}) . However, maximizing standard MI is insufficient for heterogeneous data due to its composite nature. According to Partial Information Decomposition (PID) theory [ 20 ] , information from sources 𝐗 \mathbf{X} about a target 𝐙 \mathbf{Z} can be decomposed into three distinct atoms: (1) Redundancy ( Red ) : Information shared across all modalities. (2) Uniqueness ( Uni ) : Information provided solely by a specific modality 𝐗 m \mathbf{X}_{m} . (3) Synergy ( Syn ) : Emergent information is available only when observing multiple modalities jointly and is absent in any single source. Formally, the total mutual information in this work satisfies: ℐ ⁡ ( 𝐗 , 𝐙 ) = Red ⁡ ( 𝐗 , 𝐙 ) + ∑ m ∈ { 𝐩 , 𝐠 , 𝐭 } Uni ⁡ ( 𝐗 m , 𝐙 ) + Syn ⁡ ( 𝐗 , 𝐙 ) \mathcal{I}(\mathbf{X};\mathbf{Z})=\mathrm{Red}\,(\mathbf{X};\mathbf{Z})+\textstyle\sum_{m\in\{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{g},\mathbf{t}\}}\mathrm{Uni}\,(\mathbf{X}_{m};\mathbf{Z})+\mathrm{Syn}\,(\mathbf{X};\mathbf{Z}) (2) standard fusion methods often maximize Red , as it represents the “least common denominator” features while causing modality collapse. In contrast, clinical diagnosis relies on Syn to integrate complementary cues for a holistic conclusion. Φ ​ ID \mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID} objective.

To promote the emergence of Syn and mitigates the subspace collapse of Red , We denote omni-modal synergistic interaction as Φ \mathrm{\Phi} , computed via the “ whole-minus-sum ” residual in PID to isolate multimodal information: Φ ⁡ ( { 𝐩 , 𝐠 , 𝐭 } → 𝐙 mm ) ​ = △ ​ ℐ ⁡ ( 𝐗 joint , 𝐙 mm ) ⏟ Total correlation − ∑ m ∈ { 𝐩 , 𝐠 , 𝐭 } ℐ ⁡ ( 𝐗 m , 𝐙 mm ) ⏟ Marginal redundancy \mathrm{\Phi}\left(\{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{g},\mathbf{t}\}\rightarrow\mathbf{Z}_{\text{mm}}\right)\overset{\triangle}{=}\underbrace{\mathcal{I}\left(\mathbf{X}_{\text{joint}};\mathbf{Z}_{\text{mm}}\right)}_{\text{Total correlation}}-\sum_{m\in\{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{g},\mathbf{t}\}}\underbrace{\mathcal{I}\left(\mathbf{X}_{m};\mathbf{Z}_{\text{mm}}\right)}_{\text{Marginal redundancy}} (3) where maximizing Φ \mathrm{\Phi} forces the model to capture high-order Syn interactions while minimizing the marginal Red that can be inferred from single modality. Gaussian Canonical Projector. To ensure computational tractability for estimating MI in high dimensions, we design Gaussian Canonical Projector ( GCP ) inspired by [ 22 ] . GCP leverages Layer Normalization to explicitly map heterogeneous embeddings 𝐡 ∈ { 𝐗 joint , 𝐗 m , 𝐙 mm } \mathbf{h}\in\{\mathbf{X}_{\text{joint}},\mathbf{X}_{m},\mathbf{Z}_{\text{mm}}\} onto a smooth Gaussian latent space for differential entropy estimation, enables H ⁡ ( 𝐙 ) \mathrm{H}\left(\mathbf{Z}\right) to be estimated via a parametric variational Gaussian approximation with a closed-form log-determinant: 𝐙 = 𝚷 GCP ​ ( 𝐡 ) ​ = △ ​ Sigmoid ​ ( LN ⁡ ( 𝐖 ⋅ 𝐡 ) ) , H ⁡ ( 𝐙 ) = 1 2 ​ log ​ det ( Σ 𝐙 ) \mathbf{Z}=\mathbf{\Pi}_{\text{GCP}}\big(\mathbf{h}\big)\overset{\triangle}{=}\text{Sigmoid}\Big(\mathrm{LN}\big(\mathbf{W}\cdot\mathbf{h}\big)\Big),\quad\mathrm{H}\left(\mathbf{Z}\right)=\frac{1}{2}\log\det\big(\mathrm{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{Z}}\big) (4) where 1 2 ​ log ​ det ( Σ 𝐙 ) \frac{1}{2}\log\det\left(\mathrm{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{Z}}\right) captures feature “volume”, maximized to expand info

rmation and prevent collapse. Σ 𝐙 = 1 B ​ 𝐙 ⊤ ​ 𝐙 + ϵ ​ 𝐈 \mathrm{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{Z}}=\frac{1}{\text{B}}\mathbf{Z}^{\top}\mathbf{Z}+\epsilon\mathbf{I} is the empirical covariance matrix for batch size B , 𝐈 \mathbf{I} is the identity matrix with ϵ = 10 − 5 \epsilon=10^{-5} for numerical stability. 2.4 Pretraining Objective Cross-modal contrastive alignment. We align the latent space via a symmetric InfoNCE objective [ 3 ] . Defining the directional pairwise loss ℓ ⁡ ( 𝐮 , 𝐯 ) \ell(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v}) between a query modality 𝐮 \mathbf{u} and a key modality 𝐯 \mathbf{v} , the omni-modal symmetric contrastive alignment objective is calculated as: ℒ SymCL = 1 2 ∑ k ∈ { 𝐠 , 𝐭 } ( ℓ ( 𝐩 , 𝐤 ) + ℓ ( 𝐤 , 𝐩 ) ) , ℓ ( 𝐮 , 𝐯 ) = − 1 B ∑ i = 1 B log e τ ​ 𝐮 i ⊤ ​ 𝐯 i ∑ j = 1 M e τ ​ 𝐮 j ⊤ ​ 𝐯 j \mathcal{L}_{\text{SymCL}}=\frac{1}{2}\sum_{k\in\{\mathbf{g},\mathbf{t}\}}\Big(\ell(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{k})+\ell(\mathbf{k},\mathbf{p})\Big),\ell(\mathbf{u},\mathbf{v})=-\frac{1}{\text{B}}\sum_{i=1}^{\text{B}}\log\frac{e^{\tau\mathbf{u}_{i}^{\top}\mathbf{v}_{i}}}{\sum_{j=1}^{\text{M}}e^{\tau\mathbf{u}_{j}^{\top}\mathbf{v}_{j}}} (5) where τ \tau is the temperature parameter, and the summation over k = { 𝐠 , 𝐭 } k=\{\mathbf{g},\mathbf{t}\} aligns the pathology anchor (central modality) 𝐩 \mathbf{p} with both transcriptomics 𝐠 \mathbf{g} and report embeddings 𝐭 \mathbf{t} , skipping auxiliary 𝐠 \mathbf{g} - 𝐭 \mathbf{t} alignment for efficiency. Synergistic information disentanglement. To distill Syn , we minimize the Total Correlation (TC) of projected margins as a parametric variational proxy for Eq. (3). This approximation compresses redundancy, forcing the joint embedding to capture synergistic interactions.

The loss for Φ ​ ID \mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID} objective is formulated as: ℒ Φ ​ ID = − Φ = ∑ m ∈ { 𝐩 , 𝐠 , 𝐭 } H ⁡ ( 𝐙 m ) − H ⁡ ( 𝐙 joint ) \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID}}=-\mathrm{\Phi}=\textstyle\sum_{m\in\{\mathbf{p},\mathbf{g},\mathbf{t}\}}\mathrm{H}\left(\mathbf{Z}_{m}\right)-\mathrm{H}\left(\mathbf{Z}_{\text{joint}}\right) (6) where 𝐙 ∗ = 𝚷 GCP ​ ( 𝐗 ∗ ) \mathbf{Z}_{\ast}=\mathbf{\Pi}_{\text{GCP}}(\mathbf{X}_{\ast}) . Specifically, this objective imposes a dual constraint: (1) it compresses the marginal entropies to suppress unimodal redundancy, while (2) expanding the joint entropy to capture synergistic cross-modal interactions. Complementary objective. Overall, we train Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni using a composite loss: ℒ = ℒ SymCL + γ ​ ℒ Φ ​ ID \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\text{SymCL}}+\gamma\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID}} , where the former ensures foundational semantic alignment and the latter acts as a regularizer that penalizes trivial redundancy to encourage the discovery of complementary synergistic features. We set γ = 0.2 \gamma=0.2 in this work. 3 Experimental Setups and Results 3.1 Study Design To validate Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni , we established two omni-modal pretraining cohorts by filtering TCGA 1 1 1 https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/ cases with strictly triplet-aligned modalities (pathological WSI, transcriptomics, pathology reports). For inference, only WSIs are required. Breast. For breast pretraining , we used n n =1,031 omni-modal primary breast cases from TCGA Breast Invasive Carcinoma (BRCA) cohort. Downstream evaluation was conducted on two independent cohorts: (1) BRACS dataset 2 2 2 https://www.bracs.icar.cnr.it/ ( n n =547) for 7-way breast cancer fine-grained subtyping and (2) CPTAC-BRCA 3 3 3 https://proteomic.datacommons.cancer.gov/pdc/ dataset ( n n =112) for predicting the molecular mutation status of TP53 and PIK3CA. Lung.

For lung pretraining , we used n n =919 omni-modal primary lung cases from TCGA Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer (NSCLC) cohort. We performed downstream evaluation on CPTAC-NSCLC for: (1) lung cancer subtyping (LUAD vs. LSCC, n n =604), molecular mutation prediction of (2) STK11/TP53 on CPTAC-LUAD ( n n =324), (3) ARID1A/KEAP1 on CPTAC-LSCC ( n n =304). Following [ 7 , 8 ] , we benchmark Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni against SSL models via k k -shot linear probing ( k k = 1 , 5 , 10 , 25 1,5,10,25 ) via a logistic regression classifier (L2 penalty C C = 1.0 1.0 ; max iterations= 10 4 10^{4} ) from scikit-learn. All experiments are repeated ten times by randomly sampling k k examples per class during training with different seeds, reporting the mean and standard deviation of macro-AUC. Implementation details. Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni was trained for 100 epochs (5 for warmup) using AdamW with cosine decay ( 10 − 4 10^{-4} to 10 − 8 10^{-8} ) and batch size 128. We sampled 2,048 fixed patches per slide with random oversampling applied to slides with fewer patches. All MIL models were trained from scratch with batch size of 1. Baselines. We benchmark Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni against four MIL models based on UNIv2 [ 2 ] encoder: ABMIL [ 6 ] , CLAM [ 17 ] , TransMIL [ 19 ] , and ILRA [ 27 ] . We also compare with SSL models via linear probing, including patch-level SSLs: CTransPath [ 25 ] , UNIv2 [ 2 ] , CONCH [ 16 ] , mSTAR [ 28 ] , and GPFM [ 18 ] using mean-pool embeddings (noted ∗ \ast ), and slide-levels: CHIEF [ 26 ] , TANGLE [ 7 ] , and MADELEINE [ 8 ] . 3.3 Few-shot Classification Results Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni vs. UNIv2 vs. TANGLE. Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni exceeds UNIv2 (pathology) and TANGLE (pathology + + genomic) across all tasks (Table 1 , 2 ), highlights the value of clinical (report) and biological (genomic) “views” from multimodal pretraining.

Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni vs. MILs. Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni surpasses all MILs in 8/8 tasks, achieving +4.3%, +1.2%, and +1.1% gains compared to ABMIL ( k k =25) for molecular prediction, breast and lung subtyping, respectively. Notably, Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni employs linear probing only, whereas MIL models are trained from scratch in standard few-shot settings. Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni vs. SSLs. Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni outperforms all SSL models on most tasks, often by notable margins, e.g. , +3.2% over TANGLE (BRACS, breast cancer subtyping, k k = 5 5 ) and +5.7% over UNIv2 (CPTAC-LSCC, ARID1A mutation prediction, k k = 25 25 ). Notably, this advantage holds consistently across all k k values and tasks, underscoring the excellent performance and robust generalization of Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni . We explore two key architectural features as shown in Fig. 2 . (a) the network for slide encoding: we compare ABMIL w/ pre-attention with MLP, TransMIL, and ABMIL, our choice yields notable improvements. (b) the module for multimodal feature fusion: we evaluate Trilinear [ 10 ] , Concat, and our SIB module, where SIB outperforms alternatives steadily for all six tasks. Loss ablation. We perform a thorough ablation of Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni loss function by retraining models with L1 objective, Mean-Squared Error (MSE), InfoNCE, symmetric contrastive objective (SymCL), and combining SymCL and Φ \mathrm{\Phi} ID (Ours). Fig. 2 (c) shows that our Φ \mathrm{\Phi} ID objective is indispensable: SymCL alone achieves strong gains over L1/MSE/InfoNCE, but combining it with Φ \mathrm{\Phi} ID unlocks synergistic improvements across all six tasks (+4.4% on BRACS-Subtyping and +7.2% on BRCA-PIK3CA), proving that explicit synergy disentanglement (not just contrastive alignment) is critical for maximizing multimodal diagnostic value. 3.5 Interpretability Analysis Attention heatmaps.

We generate attention heatmaps of Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni pretrained on lung/breast cancer (Fig. 3 (a)), which reveals spatial correspondence between high-attention regions and tumor areas, demonstrating task-agnostic supervised localization of pathological regions through multimodal pretraining. Omni-modal disentanglement. To investigate the structural properties of the learned latent space, we visualize omni-modal embeddings extracted from Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni pretrained on lung cancer via t-SNE (Fig. 3 (b)). The visualization exhibits three well-separated clusters, indicating that Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni effectively learns discriminative representations for each modality, preventing the modality collapse. Notably, the explicit connections between paired samples (“ Cross-modal Synergy ”) confirm that Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni preserves strong semantic alignment across heterogeneous modalities while maintaining the intrinsic biological and clinical correlations. We perform a thorough ablation of Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni loss function by retraining models with L1 objective, Mean-Squared Error (MSE), InfoNCE, symmetric contrastive objective (SymCL), and combining SymCL and Φ \mathrm{\Phi} ID (Ours). Fig. 2 (c) shows that our Φ \mathrm{\Phi} ID objective is indispensable: SymCL alone achieves strong gains over L1/MSE/InfoNCE, but combining it with Φ \mathrm{\Phi} ID unlocks synergistic improvements across all six tasks (+4.4% on BRACS-Subtyping and +7.2% on BRCA-PIK3CA), proving that explicit synergy disentanglement (not just contrastive alignment) is critical for maximizing multimodal diagnostic value. 4 Conclusion In this paper, we introduce Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni , a novel SSL framework that advances omni-modal slide representation learning by shifting the focus from redundancy-driven contrastive alignment to synergistic information disentanglement. Derived from Partial Information Decomposition (PID) theory, our proposed SIB module and Φ ​ ID \mathrm{\Phi}\text{ID} objective provide a mathematically principled mechanism to extract high-order diagnostic insights that are absent in any single modality. Extensive experiments across six benchmarks demonstrate that Φ \mathrm{\Phi} -Omni not only achieves state-of-the-art few-shot performance but maintains biologically grounded interpretability. This work highlights the power of distilling synergistic interaction from omni-modal histology, genomics, and pathology reports, paving the way for data-efficient and robust multimodal frameworks in computational pathology.
